reconstructed_statement: Given a field \(k\), a finite chain of \(k\)-modules \(V_0 \to \cdots \to V_N\) with edge maps \(f_e : V_e \to V_{e+1}\), and a family of submodules \(P_t \le V_t\), \(\mathrm{HasBarcode}\ V\ f\ P\) is the proposition that \(P\) is presented by finitely many interval-supported barcode lines. Concretely, there must be a natural number \(M\), birth and death vertices \(b_\lambda,d_\lambda : \mathrm{Fin}\ M \to \mathrm{Fin}(N+1)\) with \(b_\lambda\le d_\lambda\), and vectors \(\ell_\lambda(t)\in V_t\) such that \(\ell_\lambda(t)=0\) outside the interval \([b_\lambda,d_\lambda]\), \(\ell_\lambda(t)\ne 0\) on that interval, the edge maps carry \(\ell_\lambda(e)\) to \(\ell_\lambda(e+1)\) while the interval is alive, the edge maps send it to zero after its death, and for every vertex \(t\) the one-dimensional submodules \(k\cdot \ell_\lambda(t)\) are independent and span exactly \(P_t\). This is the Lean encoding of an internal direct-sum decomposition of \(P\) into interval-module summands.
summary: Predicate asserting that a family of submodules is an internal direct sum of finitely many interval-supported barcode lines.

In the formal development it bridges `rankPattern d A` to counts of barcode-like intervals: its dependencies include the tuple barcode theorem, the comparison between `rankPattern` and the finrank of a composed-map range, and a theorem computing that finrank from interval lines. Its listed user `DLNFibre.Core.rankPattern_eq_cumul_barMult` consumes the witnesses to express the same rank pattern through `barMult` and `cumul` data.
reconstructed_statement: For every field \(k\), natural number \(N\), dimension function \(d : \mathrm{Fin}(N+1) \to \mathbb{N}\), and tuple \(A : \mathrm{DLNFibre.Core.Tuple}\ d\), there exist a natural number \(M\) and functions \(\mathrm{birth}, \mathrm{death} : \mathrm{Fin}\ M \to \mathrm{Fin}(N+1)\) such that: first, \(\mathrm{birth}(\lambda) \le \mathrm{death}(\lambda)\) for every \(\lambda : \mathrm{Fin}\ M\); second, for every \(t : \mathrm{Fin}(N+1)\), the number of indices \(\lambda\) with \(\mathrm{birth}(\lambda) \le t \le \mathrm{death}(\lambda)\) is exactly \(d(t)\); and third, for every \(i,j : \mathrm{Fin}(N+1)\) with \(i \le j\), \(\mathrm{DLNFibre.Core.rankPattern}\ d\ A\ i\ j\) is exactly the number of indices \(\lambda\) with \(\mathrm{birth}(\lambda) \le i\) and \(j \le \mathrm{death}(\lambda)\).
